lens: Content accuracy & staleness (30 Oct 2026). Sampled 29 pages in full across all 7 categories plus index/README/BUILD-GUIDE/STALENESS, and grepped all 94 pages + assets/js for PoP counts, customer/MQ/SLA claims, dated and future-tense wording, and path-chip conventions. Note: a parallel commit (dc967bb, 30 Oct) changed "80+ PoPs" to "100+" on four pages and deck-content.js while this audit ran; findings below reflect the post-commit state.

findings.title: One "80+ Cato PoPs" survived the 100+ sweep (wrapped line), and the search index / prospect edition need rebuilding
findings.where: usecases/network-global-expansion.html:36 ("nearest of 80+ Cato\n PoPs" — hero lede/meta); verify with: /usr/bin/grep -rnoE '\b80\+[^<]{0,40}' usecases | grep -i cato. Also assets/search-index (built by _extract/build-search.py) and ../catoprospectlibrary (build-prospect.py) still carry pre-sweep text if not regenerated after dc967bb.
findings.problem: Commit dc967bb updated 9 occurrences to "100+ PoPs" but the lede on the Global Expansion page wraps "80+ Cato" / "PoPs" across two source lines, so a single-line regex missed it. The same page now says 100+ in its stat tile, diagram, figcaption and gotcha but 80+ in its opening sentence — a contradiction within one page. The full-text search index and the derived prospect edition are generated artefacts and will keep serving "80+" until rebuilt.
findings.proposal: Change line 36 to "nearest of 100+ Cato PoPs"; then run python3 _extract/build-search.py and python3 _extract/build-prospect.py and commit both. Add a multi-line-safe check to verify.sh: python3 -c that strips tags, collapses whitespace and asserts no '80+ PoP' / '80+ Cato' remains (see finding on staleness tooling).

findings.title: Gartner MQ claim is the 2025 report; the 2026 MQ (Cato Leader, third consecutive year) is now the verified fact
findings.where: usecases/migration-cloudflare.html:109-116 ("in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SASE Platforms, Cato is a Leader (repeat placement) and Cloudflare is a Visionary — approximately 400 active enterprise SASE customers per Gartner's estimate") and the gotcha card "Concede PoP count gracefully — Gartner's 2025 MQ summaries ... Visionary ... ~400-customer estimate" (~line 214 in extracted text). Same text is duplicated in assets/js/deck-content.js for the cloudflare deck. STALENESS.md row "2025 Gartner MQ ... | On next MQ publication (~annual)".
findings.problem: The 2026 Gartner MQ for SASE Platforms was published 31 Jul 2026 with Cato a Leader for the third consecutive year, so the register's own trigger fired three months ago. The page still cites the 2025 edition for Cato's placement, Cloudflare's placement and the ~400-customer estimate — the last two are competitive claims that must be re-read from the 2026 report, not carried forward, or they become unattributable in front of a prospect. "Repeat placement" undersells the verified "third consecutive year".
findings.proposal: Update Cato's line to "a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SASE Platforms — the third consecutive year". Re-verify Cloudflare's 2026 placement and whether Gartner restated a customer-count estimate; if not re-verifiable, drop the ~400 figure rather than keep a 2025 number beside a 2026 citation. Mirror the change in deck-content.js, and move the STALENESS row's "last verified" to 30 Oct 2026 with next trigger Jul 2027.

findings.title: No single source of platform facts — PoP count, SLA, customer count and MQ status are hand-typed in HTML, SVG text, img alt and deck JS, and two verified facts appear nowhere
findings.where: PoP count: 9 sites across 4 pages + deck-content.js:51,858 (just swept by hand); 99.999% SLA: network-sdwan.html stat row + table, network-resilient-site-design.html:133, access-app-connectors.html:136 (SVG), deck-content.js:560, security-compliance NIS2 table; customer count (>4,800, 27 Jul 2026 ARR release): zero occurrences (grep -rniE '[0-9,]+\+? customers' usecases finds only Sophos/SonicWall's own counts); MQ Leader: only the stale negative-framing mention on migration-cloudflare; the only analyst quote on a Field-ready page is "Gartner, Strategic Roadmap for Networking, 2019" (management-visibility.html:28-32). README calls assets/js/deck-content.js "generated" but no _extract script emits it (grep -l deck-content.js _extract/*.py → only build-prospect.py, which strips it).
findings.problem: The 30 Oct PoP sweep had to touch four pages, an SVG , an , two figcaptions and a JS file — and still missed one line. Every platform-level number is a maintenance fan-out, which is exactly why the register's "80+ PoPs — semi-annually" row sat unactioned from July to October. Meanwhile the two strongest verified proof points (4,800+ customers; MQ Leader three years running) are absent from a sales-enablement library, and the one analyst citation on the flagship visibility page is seven years old.
findings.proposal: Create assets/js/platform-facts.js: window.UC_FACTS = { pops: "100+", backboneSla: "99.999%", customers: "4,800+", mq: "Leader — 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SASE Platforms (third consecutive year)", asOf: "2026-10-30", sources: {...} }. In app.js, on DOMContentLoaded fill every element with data-fact="pops" etc. (works for <span> in prose/figcaptions and for SVG <text> nodes; file:// safe, no fetch). Convert the ~15 existing hard-coded sites to data-fact spans with the current value as fallback text (so no-JS still reads correctly). Have deck-content.js read UC_FACTS at deck-build time instead of literal strings. Add a compact "Platform at a glance" strip (customers · PoPs · SLA · MQ) to index.html's "New to the library?" journey and replace the 2019 Gartner quote on management-visibility with the 2026 MQ line. Replace the STALENESS PoP row with one row pointing at platform-facts.js.

findings.title: "New" badge on 79 of 94 pages has stopped carrying information — the catalog has no added-date to age it
findings.where: assets/js/catalog.js: grep -oE 'status: *"[a-z]*"' assets/js/catalog.js | sort | uniq -c → 79 new / 13 ready / 3 wip. index.html legend: "New — added with this library". assets/js/app.js:18 STATUS.new → badge-new "New". Git add dates: access-third-party & network-sdwan 2026-07-18, migration-sonicwall 2026-08-29, security-iso27001 2026-09-24, access-app-connectors & demo-platform-60 2026-10-14 — all wear the same badge.
findings.problem: The legend text ("added with this library") was written for a July 2026 build; 3.5 months and ~45 added pages later, a page from 18 Jul and one from 14 Oct are indistinguishable, and the badge no longer tells an SE what is actually new. Because catalog entries carry no date, the badge cannot age automatically, and "new" is also masking pages that have since been demo-verified (e.g. management-dem, access-remote-worker both say screenshots were captured from the demo tenant in July yet remain "new" rather than "ready").
findings.proposal: Add added: "YYYY-MM-DD" to every catalog entry (one-off script: for f in usecases/*.html; git log --diff-filter=A --format=%as -- $f | tail -1). In app.js render badge-new only when (today - added) ≤ 90 days, otherwise fall back to the entry's status (ready/wip). Change the legend to "New — added in the last 90 days". Sweep the 13-ready/79-new split once: promote pages whose runbook has been run against the demo tenant (those with "Status: verified against documentation" blocks or demo-tenant captures) to ready. Have whatsnew.py (already reading git history) warn when a page lacks added:.

findings.title: Three WIP/draft callouts now contradict the pages they sit on
findings.where: usecases/security-ai.html (status wip): callout "the separate AI Security PoV deck is currently an uncustomised copy of the Visibility PoV" and "Starter guidance — not yet a scripted PoV" — yet the page carries a full KB-cited PoV runbook with success-criteria table. usecases/security-compliance.html (wip): "demo runbook below is starter guidance ... not a field-validated script" above a complete PoV section with Trust Center facts checked 24 Sep 2026. usecases/security-ai-visibility.html (wip): "marked DRAFT as of 09 Apr 2026 ... details pending as of 31 Mar 2026 ... others TBD" repeated in three places.
findings.problem: The WIP wording describes the state of the source PPTX in April–July 2026, not the state of the page today. An SE reading security-ai sees "not yet a scripted PoV" immediately above a scripted PoV. The visibility-assessment page quotes a seven-month-old draft date for a live commercial offer ("no cost, limited time") without any evidence the deck or terms were rechecked. STALENESS lists only the visibility deck ("On deck update"), not the other two.
findings.proposal: Re-check the three source decks in '4 - Security use cases' and the AI PoV deck. Where the deck is still draft, keep one dated callout ("Deck still DRAFT as of <date checked>; this page's runbook was authored for the library") and delete the "not yet a scripted PoV" sentences that no longer apply. Where the deck has moved on, retire the callout and set status to ready. Add STALENESS rows for the security-ai and security-compliance WIP decks with a quarterly trigger.

findings.title: CMA path-chip convention is now split old-nav/new-nav — including inside the same demo and the same page
findings.where: Inventory: grep -rhoE '<span class="path">[^<]*' usecases | sed 's/<span class="path">//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn. Pairs: "Administration → Audit Trail" (45) vs "Account → Audit Trail" (security-iso27001.html:612,749, which states "Paths are the new-navigation CMA") vs truncated "Administration → Audit" (security-firewall-refresh.html:526, migration-palo-alto.html:632); "Access → Device Posture" (30, incl. demo-platform-60.html:74 running order and :163 staging checklist) vs "Resources → Device Posture" (demo-ztna, access-app-connectors, security-iso27001) — the 60-minute demo and its own ZTNA segment disagree; "Monitor → Experience Monitoring" (24 chips, 14 files, mostly migration-*) vs "Home → Experience Monitoring" (19+7 chips, 18 files) — both appear in management-visibility.html (~lines 139 and 234); "Monitor → Events" (160) vs "Home → Events" (14); "Assets → Device Inventory" (15) vs KB "Home → Devices"; typo "Resource → System Settings" (access-app-connectors.html:226,491). BUILD-GUIDE.md "CMA navigation paths" still prescribes the old menu (Monitor → …, Access → Device Posture, Assets → Device Inventory, Administration → Audit Trail).
findings.problem: STALENESS records this as "confirm against the live CMA, then align library-wide in one sweep", but since then the newest pages (Oct 2026) have adopted new-nav piecemeal, so the library now teaches two menus. An SE following demo-platform-60's running order is sent to Access → Device Posture, then the linked segment page sends them to Resources → Device Posture. BUILD-GUIDE keeps minting old-nav chips in every new page.
findings.proposal: Pick new-nav (it is what the live CMA, the newest pages and the KB use). Write the mapping into BUILD-GUIDE (Monitor → Events ⇒ Home → Events; Monitor → Experience Monitoring ⇒ Home → Experience Monitoring; Access → Device Posture ⇒ Resources → Device Posture; Administration → Audit Trail ⇒ Account → Audit Trail; Assets → Device Inventory ⇒ Home → Devices; Administration → API & Integrations ⇒ Resources → Service API Keys / Event Integrations; Resource → ⇒ Resources →). Apply with one reviewed sed pass over usecases/*.html and deck-content.js, then add a verify.sh check that extracts all chips and fails on any top-level menu outside the allowed set {Home, Network, Security, Access, Resources, Account, AI Security, Monitor(only if kept), Site Configuration, Notifications}. Regenerate search index and prospect edition.

findings.title: Two DEM pages cite different Client minimums for the same Connection Details nodes; EM version gates are a quarter past their recheck
findings.where: usecases/access-remote-worker.html:245 & 327 "device, Wi-Fi and LAN gateway nodes in Connection Details need Windows v5.11 / macOS v5.7" vs usecases/management-dem.html:106, 270, 517, 642 "Device, Wi-Fi and LAN gateway nodes need the Client ... Windows v5.12.10 / macOS v5.7 or higher". Both pages say the thresholds were "verified in July 2026" and "re-check before quoting". Related drift: access-hybrid-workforce.html:394 "Continuous posture checks ... (10 minutes is the recommended setting)" vs security-iso27001 "enabled by default for all accounts since 7 August 2026 ... needs Windows 5.15+ / macOS 5.9+".
findings.problem: Same KB fact, two numbers (5.11 vs 5.12.10) on sibling pages that cross-link each other — an SE quoting one in a proposal can be contradicted by the other. STALENESS has the Always-On gates under access-remote-worker and the probe gates under the PoV row but not the Connection Details node gates, and all were due a quarterly recheck in October. The hybrid-workforce posture sentence predates the Aug 2026 default-on change and omits the Client gate the ISO page documents.
findings.proposal: Re-fetch KB "Experience Monitoring Connection Details" / "What is Cato Experience Monitoring" via the .md route (per memory kb-access.md), align both pages to the current minimum, and update the 'verified' stamps. Update access-hybrid-workforce:394 to "continuous checks are on by default (10-minute interval, since 7 Aug 2026; Windows 5.15+ / macOS 5.9+)". Add one STALENESS row "EM Connection Details node and underlay-probe Client gates" listing both pages so the next sweep edits them together.

findings.title: Cisco page still frames Aug/Sep 2026 EOS dates as upcoming; the AnyConnect sibling already says they have passed
findings.where: usecases/migration-cisco.html:43-46 stat tiles under "Forced transitions — Cisco's own calendar sets the timeline": "Aug 2026 ASA 5506-X / 5508-X / 5516-X end of support", "Sep 2026 Umbrella legacy SKUs end of software maintenance"; table rows :53-54 (31 Aug 2026, 30 Sep 2026); intro "Each milestone below is a forced project inside the Cisco portfolio". Compare usecases/migration-anyconnect.html:26-28 "reached end of support on 31 August 2026 — those boxes are now running unsupported".
findings.problem: As of 30 Oct 2026 two of the four headline tiles describe events in the past but the surrounding prose ("forced project", "calendar sets the timeline") reads as forward-looking. The sibling page was reframed on 27 Sep; this one was not, so the two Cisco pages disagree in tense about the same ASA date. STALENESS says the cisco tiles "already read as dates" — true, but the framing sentence does not.
findings.proposal: Reframe the two tiles and rows as past ("EOS 31 Aug 2026 — unsupported today"; "EOSM 30 Sep 2026 — TAC only to 2030"), add a small .stat-past marker (or "passed" sub-label) convention in style.css for any dated stat tile whose date has gone, and change the intro to "two of these have already passed". Update the STALENESS Umbrella row ("EOS Sep 2025" → add "EOSM 30 Sep 2026 passed").

findings.title: SonicWall page's EOS-driven wave sequencing is now in the past — and the page has no STALENESS rows at all
findings.where: usecases/migration-sonicwall.html:47 stat tile "2026 1 Aug: TZ400/TZ600/NSA 3600/NSa 3650 end of support — the classic Gen 6 branch estate goes dark for fixes"; :200-202 "Sequence the waves by the EOS calendar: the 16 Apr 2026 models and the Aug 2026 TZ400/600 wave first — those boxes must be replaced with something regardless"; :271-272 same advice in the co-existence callout. grep -n -i sonicwall _extract/STALENESS.md → no match (page added 29 Aug 2026).
findings.problem: Both dates have passed, so advice to "put them in the first Socket waves" should now read "these are already unsupported — lead with them". The page is dense with dated, fast-moving claims (SMA 100 retirement 31 Oct 2025, MySonicWall breach concluded 8 Oct 2025, Akira proceeds ~$244M by Sep 2025, CVE-2024-40766, Gen 8 shipping, Nov 2025 state-actor attribution) yet none is in the register, contrary to README's "update it when adding dated claims" rule — so nothing will trigger a recheck.
findings.proposal: Reframe :47 and :200-202/:271 to past tense. Add two STALENESS rows: (1) SonicWall EOS calendar (Gen 6 LRM 20 Apr 2024, 31 Jul 2025, 16 Apr 2026, 1 Aug 2026 — all past; Gen 8 shipping) — recheck quarterly for new EOS notices; (2) SonicWall incident set (CVE-2024-40766 KEV, Aug 2025 Gen 7 campaign, MySonicWall breach + Mandiant 8 Oct 2025, Akira figures, attribution reporting) — quarterly, watch for new advisories/attributions.

findings.title: Several register triggers have fired but the pages still carry the pre-trigger wording
findings.where: security-healthcare-nhs.html:53-61 "Checked 27 September 2026 ... verify ... the updated audit guidance NHS England said would land in early October 2026" and the 47-outcome count "carried over from v8 and NOT yet re-verified" (STALENESS trigger: Oct 2026). ai-eu-ai-act.html:24-38, :80, :376 "publication was still pending as this page was written" / "omnibus awaiting Official Journal publication" (trigger: "On OJ publication (~weeks)" from Jul 2026). ai-homegrown-apps.html: 15 occurrences of "verified 23 Jul 2026" and "not locatable in the public docs index as of 23 July 2026" for Outposts/Playground/Interaction Explorer (trigger: quarterly on the register's self-described fastest-moving surface; the 26 Sep sweep established these docs are login-gated, not absent). security-iso27001 "since 7 August 2026" ×5 (trigger: reframe as settled history).
findings.problem: The register works only if someone reads it; four rows are past due and the on-page text still says "pending", "would land in early October", or "not locatable" when the Sep sweep already found the real state (gated). Hard-coded "in 2026" strings (demo-casb.html:78 "every audience recognises in 2026"; migration-sonicwall.html:65) will rot on 1 Jan 2027 with no trigger at all.
findings.proposal: Do the four rechecks now (NHS v9 outcome count + audit guidance; OJ publication of the AI omnibus — cite the amending regulation and drop "pending"; AI-apps KB via logged-in browser, replacing "not locatable" with "login-gated, see KB access note"; ISO "since 7 Aug 2026" → "continuous by default"). Then build _extract/staleness-check.py: parse STALENESS.md rows, extract any month/year in the "Recheck when" cell, print rows whose date ≤ today, and grep the named pages for a configurable list of rot patterns ("still pending", "would land", "as of \d+ \w+ 2026" older than 90 days, "in 2026\b", "this year", "80\+ PoP"). Wire it into verify.sh as a warn-only 9th check so every monthly pass surfaces overdue rows.

findings.title: README and register header carry build-time counts and dates that no longer match the tree
findings.where: README.md:9 "57 KB-grounded PoV runbooks" — actual: grep -l 'id="pov"' usecases/*.html | wc -l → 64. README footer "Built July 2026". _extract/STALENESS.md header "All dates were verified at build time (July 2026)" with no last-full-review stamp. _extract/BUILD-GUIDE.md CMA path list (old-nav, see chip finding) and its "Allowed external URLs" list omits knowledge.catonetworks.com pages now cited on most new pages except via the "any URL you have fetched" clause.
findings.problem: Documentation facts drift silently: the PoV count is seven short, the register claims a July verification baseline although ~20 rows were verified in Sep/Oct, and a new page author following BUILD-GUIDE will reproduce the old nav. These are the files the README tells maintainers to trust.
findings.proposal: Fix the PoV count and add a maintained "Last full staleness review: <date>" line at the top of STALENESS.md. Have verify.sh (or whatsnew.py) assert README's page count and PoV count against catalog.js and the id="pov" grep, failing on mismatch. Refresh BUILD-GUIDE's CMA path section per the chip finding and add the KB .md-route verification habit from memory kb-access.md as an explicit step.

findings.title: Private Access page is the only place stating "100+ PoPs · 99.999% SLA" inside an SVG — now consistent, but SVG-embedded facts are invisible to text sweeps
findings.where: usecases/access-app-connectors.html:136 (spotlight SVG <text> "100+ PoPs · 99.999% SLA"); management-visibility.html:186 and network-global-expansion.html:167 (dg-tiny SVG text with PoP counts); assets/js/deck-diagrams.js (diagram JSON carrying the same strings, e.g. "Global Private Backbone — … PoP locations"); assets/img/pop-map.png alt text on three pages.
findings.problem: Facts embedded as SVG text and diagram JSON are rendered graphics, so a reader comparing pages sees the number, but grep-based sweeps on prose patterns (and the full-text search index, which indexes page text) treat them differently; until today this page said 100+ while three others said 80+ for three weeks. The same risk applies to the SLA and any future count.
findings.proposal: Covered structurally by the platform-facts finding (data-fact on SVG <text>), plus: extend build-diagrams.py / deck-diagrams.js generation to source these strings from UC_FACTS, and add the SVG-text and alt-text scan to the staleness-check script so a fact change is verified in markup, diagrams and images in one run.

lens: UX & Navigation — how a new SE finds the right page in 30 seconds (index, planner, whatsnew + 10 pages shot headless at 1440 and 390px, light and dark; app.js / style.css / catalog.js / build-search.py read in full)

findings.title: Search box sits two screens below the fold on the index
findings.where: index.html lines 51–123 (Start-here grid, deck-builder card, then .filter-bar). Measured at 1440×900: #uc-search top = 1706px, first .uc-card = 1922px; page is 14,159px tall. At 390px the 9-link topnav wraps to 4 rows (mob-index.png) pushing the hero down ~190px.
findings.problem: The primary way-finding tool (full-text search + category/vertical filters) is reached only after scrolling past the hero, five Start-here cards and the deck builder. A new SE's 30 seconds are spent scrolling, not searching. The filter bar is also not sticky, so once you are inside the 38-card Migration block you have to scroll ~10k px back up to refine.
findings.proposal: Move #uc-search into the hero (.hero-home) as a large search field with the category buttons under it; make the Start-here grid and the deck-builder card <details> blocks that remember their open/closed state in localStorage (collapsed by default after the first visit); make .filter-bar `position: sticky; top: 56px` with a surface background and a compact single-row layout once scrolled (toggle a .compact class on scrollY > 400). Keep the result-count next to the search.

findings.title: Full-text search is a substring match over a flattened word blob — 'ips' returns 79 of 94 pages
findings.where: assets/js/app.js initIndex → matches() (lines 32–38): `hay.indexOf(t) !== -1` over title+summary+tags+UC_SEARCH[id]; _extract/build-search.py page_words() emits one space-joined string of every unique token (719 KB). Probed: ips→79 cards, dem→87, ztna→48, pci→22.
findings.problem: Short terms hit inside longer words (ips matches chips/relationships/tips; dem matches demo/demonstrate), so common SE queries return almost the whole library with no ranking, no highlight and no indication of why a card matched. Category order is preserved, so the best title match can be the 60th card.
findings.proposal: (1) Match on word boundaries: build-search already sorts unique words — split once into a Set per page at load (or regex `(^|\s)term`), and treat a query token as a prefix match on words (ztn→ztna) not an infix. (2) Score: title hit 8, tag 4, summary 2, vertical 2, body 1; when state.q is non-empty render a single flat 'Best matches' grid sorted by score above the category sections (or collapse categories). (3) Wrap matched substrings in title/summary with <mark> and add a small 'matches page text' chip when only the body matched. (4) Have build-search.py also emit per-page h2 headings so the chip can say 'in: Troubleshooting'.

findings.title: No URL state: searches and filters cannot be shared, #cat anchors scroll but do not filter, hero tags are dead text
findings.where: assets/js/app.js initIndex (state object line 29, render() lines 52–72) never reads location.search or writes history; index.html topnav links 21–27 are `#cat-*` anchors; usecases/*.html hero tags are plain <span class="tag"> (e.g. access-third-party.html:40–41) while index card tags are clickable (app.js 76–85).
findings.problem: An SE cannot send a colleague 'all Retail pages' or 'search: QUIC'; clicking Security in the topnav jumps to the heading but leaves 94 cards rendered; tags on a use-case page look identical to the clickable ones on the index but do nothing. The prospect edition inherits the same dead ends.
findings.proposal: In render(): `history.replaceState(null,'', '?'+new URLSearchParams({q,cat,vert}).toString())` (omit defaults) and on init hydrate state from location.search, pressing the matching .filter-btn. Change topnav category links to `index.html?cat=Security#cat-security` and hero tags on pages to `<a class="tag" href="../index.html?q=ZTNA">` (BUILD-GUIDE + a one-off sed over usecases/*.html). Vertical filter gets `?vert=`. Add `scroll-margin-top: 80px` to `.category-h h2` so anchor jumps clear the sticky topnav.

findings.title: Add keyboard shortcuts and a library-wide quick-switcher (Cmd/Ctrl-K)
findings.where: assets/js/app.js — only keydown handlers are Escape (lightbox, feedback) and ArrowLeft/Right inside .phase-player; use-case page topnav offers only '← All use cases' (access-third-party.html:22). catalog.js (94 entries) is already loaded on every page.
findings.problem: From any of the 94 pages the only route to another page is back to the index or the two pager links. Power users (SEs mid-demo) have no way to jump by typing.
findings.proposal: New initQuickSwitcher() in app.js: `/` focuses #uc-search on the index; Cmd/Ctrl-K (and a topnav button 'Search ⌘K' inserted before .spacer on every page) opens a .qs-overlay with an input that fuzzy-matches catalog title+tags+category (prefix/subsequence scoring, no body text needed), shows up to 8 rows with category chip + status, Up/Down/Enter to open, Esc to close; `g i` goes to index, `[` / `]` follow the pager. Reuse .fb-overlay/.fb-dialog styles. Strip nothing for prospect — it only reads catalog.js.

findings.title: Status badge has collapsed — 79 of 94 cards say 'New'
findings.where: assets/js/catalog.js status field: 79 new / 13 ready / 3 wip (grep -c). Rendered top-right of every card (app.js cardHTML lines 40–50) and in every hero; legend in index.html lines 42–46.
findings.problem: The badge takes the most prominent slot on the card but carries almost no information; 'New' is meaningless three months on and does not tell an SE what actually matters before a demo: are there real CMA captures, is there a PoV runbook, is a capture still outstanding.
findings.proposal: Derive evidence badges automatically instead of hand-set status: extend _extract/build-search.py (it already parses every page) to emit assets/js/catalog-meta.js with {shots: n, placeholders: n, pov: bool, talkTrack: bool, words: n, sections: n}. cardHTML renders a compact icon row (📷 8 · 🧪 PoV · 🎬 Demo) and the badge becomes 'Demo-verified' (shots>0 && placeholders==0) / 'Captures wanted' / 'In development'. Add an `added: "2026-10-14"` date to catalog entries and show 'New' only for 60 days. Update the index legend accordingly.

findings.title: Card density: 258 distinct tags (197 used once), unbounded summaries, up to 7 tags per card
findings.where: assets/js/catalog.js tags arrays (max 7 per entry; 197 singletons); app.js cardHTML (lines 40–50); style.css .uc-card p (line 484) has no clamp; .uc-grid minmax(300px) (line 470).
findings.problem: Clicking a tag (the advertised discovery path) mostly returns exactly one card because three-quarters of tags are unique; cards vary from 230 to 330px tall so rows look ragged; the eye has nothing stable to scan (category chip, badge, title, 3–5 line summary, 5–8 tags, CTA).
findings.proposal: Add a tag canon (_extract/TAGS.md: ~60 approved tags with synonyms) and a verify.sh check that flags singleton tags; show max 4 tags on the card with a '+3' pill that expands on hover/focus; `display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:3` on .uc-card p with the full summary in the title attribute; move the vertical pill into .uc-top next to the category chip; add the evidence/reading-time meta row from the finding above. Hide the redundant 'Open use case →' CTA when a meta row is present.

findings.title: Reading time and last-verified date are never shown
findings.where: Pages range 889 words (migration-journey-mpls.html) to 6,687 words (security-iso27001.html); `grep -l 'Last verified\|Last updated' usecases/*.html` = 0 pages; _extract/STALENESS.md holds dated facts but nothing surfaces on the page; whatsnew.html is the only trace of change dates.
findings.problem: An SE opening a page before a call cannot tell if it is a 4-minute read or a 30-minute playbook, nor whether the KB-dependent claims were checked this quarter. Trust in a field library depends on both.
findings.proposal:
build-search.py (or a sibling build-meta.py) writes `words` and `lastCommit` (from `git log -1 --format=%cs -- usecases/x.html`) into catalog-meta.js; app.js initPage inserts `
≈ 14 min read · Updated 27 Sep 2026 · Verified against KB 27 Sep 2026
` under the hero tag row (verified date from a `data-verified="YYYY-MM-DD"` body attribute that STALENESS sweeps bump). Cards show '14 min' in the meta row. Prospect build keeps both.

findings.title: Related-pages strip computed from the catalog, above the pager
findings.where: Every page ends with a hand-written 'In this library' card inside #resources (2 links on management-api-automation.html, 9 on demo-platform-60.html) followed by #pager (app.js initPage lines 150–161). No cross-category discovery exists anywhere else.
findings.problem: Related links are maintained by hand, drift as pages are added (App Connectors, Platform Demo segments are referenced by few older pages), and sit below the fold of a 9k-px page. Vertical siblings (Retail PCI ↔ Retail store networks) are never surfaced automatically.
findings.proposal: initPage builds `.related-strip` (3–4 mini cards reusing .uc-card at reduced padding) from catalog: score = shared tags ×2 + same vertical ×3 + same category ×1 − pager neighbours; insert before #pager with kicker 'Related use cases'. Keep the manual list for curated links. Add a 'Show in library' link to `../index.html?cat=…`.

findings.title: Pager wraps across categories and around the whole 94-page ring
findings.where: assets/js/app.js initPage pager (lines 150–161): `prev = CAT[(idx-1+len)%len]`. Seen on access-third-party.html: Previous = 'Demo Segment: Digital Experience Monitoring' (Platform Demo), Next = 'Securing the Hybrid Workforce'.
findings.problem: Prev/Next implies a sequence but the sequence is catalogue order, so the first Access page's 'previous' is the last Platform Demo segment and Migration policy deep-dives alternate with vendor playbooks. The SE has no sense of position ('3 of 15 Security pages').
findings.proposal: Filter CAT to the page's category before computing neighbours; show `.dir` as 'Previous · Security 2 of 15' and add a centre link '↑ All Security use cases' to `../index.html?cat=Security`. For migration-*-policy pages pair prev/next with their vendor playbook (same prefix) via a `group:` field in catalog.js. Hide the pager at the ends rather than wrapping.

findings.title: TOC: no mobile fallback, sentence-length labels, no progress or back-to-top on 9–12k px pages
findings.where: assets/css/style.css:164 hides .toc under 900px with nothing in its place (mob-page.png); labels are raw h2 text (app.js initPage lines 128–132) e.g. 'Where “the app is slow” tickets go to die' wrapping to 3 lines; scroll-spy rootMargin -15%/-70% (line 145) keeps the last link active after the last section scrolls out; pages are 7–12k px tall (p-method.png 12,120px).
findings.problem: On a laptop at a customer site (narrow window, projector mirroring) the TOC vanishes entirely; on desktop the sticky TOC becomes a wall of wrapped text on 11-section pages (migration-sonicwall-policy.html); there is no way to tell how far through a page you are or to get back to the hero buttons (Print, Intro deck).
findings.proposal: (1) Inject a `<details class="toc-mobile"><summary>On this page</summary>…</details>` above <main> when width < 900px (CSS shows one or the other). (2) Support `<h2 data-toc="Short label">`; fallback truncates at 38 chars. (3) Add a 3px `.read-progress` bar at the bottom edge of .topnav driven by scrollY/(scrollHeight-innerHeight). (4) A fixed '↑ Top' pill (bottom-left, hidden until scrollY > 1200, respects .deck-tray at bottom-right). (5) In the observer, mark the nearest section when none intersects.

findings.title: Demo/PoV tab bar: not keyboard-navigable, not persistent, scrolls away above 2,600-px runbooks
findings.where: assets/js/app.js initRunbookTabs (lines 165–208): role=tablist/tab set but no ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End handler, no aria-controls/ids; active tab resets to Demo on every page unless #pov is in the hash; style.css:414 .rb-tabs is static. management-dem.html #demo = 2,641px tall; PoV sections are longer.
findings.problem: An SE in PoV mode re-clicks the PoV tab on all 64 pages that have one; keyboard users cannot switch tabs with arrows as the ARIA pattern promises; deep in a runbook the tab bar is off-screen so the reader forgets which runbook they are in.
findings.proposal: Add keydown on the bar (Arrow keys cycle + focus, Home/End), set `id="rb-tab-demo"`/`aria-controls="demo"` and `aria-labelledby` on the sections; persist the last chosen tab in localStorage `uc-rb-tab` (hash still wins, default Demo); make `.rb-tabs { position: sticky; top: 56px; background: var(--page); z-index: 5 }` with the active label repeated as a small kicker; show step counts in the labels ('🎬 Demo runbook · 6 steps').

findings.title: Lightbox lacks close control, caption, scroll lock, focus management and prev/next
findings.where: assets/js/app.js initLightbox (lines 298–338 now; was 211–251): overlay closes on any click (including the image), no button, aria-modal absent, body overflow stays 'visible' (probed), focus not moved/returned; style.css:248–256. management-dem.html has 8 figure.shot images.
findings.problem: Dense CMA captures (lightbox.png) cannot be panned or zoomed further than 'fit', the figcaption that explains what to look at is not shown while enlarged, the page scrolls behind the overlay on trackpads, and screen-reader/keyboard users get a dialog with no way in or out except Escape.
findings.proposal: Add a visible `×` button (top-right, focused on open, focus returned on close), copy the figure's figcaption text under the image, set `aria-modal="true"` and `document.documentElement.style.overflow='hidden'` while open, ArrowLeft/Right to step through all figure.shot on the page with 'n / 8', wheel/double-click toggles `transform: scale(2)` with the cursor as origin, and stop click-to-close on the image itself (close on backdrop, button or Esc).

findings.title: Dark mode: CMA screenshots glare at full brightness; hero deck buttons keep light-theme borders
findings.where: assets/css/style.css:238–243 `figure.shot img { background:#fff }` with no dark override (dark block starts line 531); seen on p-tls-dark.png / management-dem dark. Dark topnav/hero otherwise consistent.
findings.problem: Light-UI PNGs on a near-black surface are the brightest thing on the page and break the reading flow; the surrounding .shot-frame navy gradient is tuned for light mode.

Add a `prefers-color-scheme` listener so the toggle repaints when the OS switches while the tab is open (initTheme only reads once).

findings.title: What's new is a 30,000-px single column of raw commit messages

findings.title: Start-here grid has an orphan card and no vertical or PoV entry point

lens: ACCESSIBILITY — index.html, planner.html, whatsnew.html, 12 sampled use-case pages (access-third-party exemplar, access-app-connectors, access-identity-design, management-dem, network-cloud-connectivity, security-iso27001, security-inbound-ips, ai-threat-landscape, migration-methodology, migration-journey-mpls, migration-cisco-asa-policy, demo-platform-60) plus library-wide greps over all 94 pages, assets/css/style.css tokens (contrast computed) and assets/js/app.js / deck-export.js. Diagrams score well (120/120 SVGs carry role="img" with title/desc or aria-label, no duplicate ids, all 305 images have descriptive non-duplicate alt text, reduced-motion is honoured globally). The defects are in keyboard operability of the injected UI, heading hierarchy, focus/contrast tokens, and table/link semantics.

findings.title: Demo/PoV runbook tabs are a keyboard dead-end
findings.where: assets/js/app.js initRunbookTabs (committed lines 165–208; `btns[t.id].setAttribute("tabindex", on ? "0" : "-1")`), affects the 57 pages with both section#demo and section#pov
findings.problem: The inactive tab gets tabindex=-1 (roving-tabindex pattern) but no ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End keydown handler exists, so a keyboard or switch user can never reach the PoV tab from the tab bar. The tablist also lacks aria-controls on tabs and role="tabpanel"/aria-labelledby on the two sections, and the tab labels start with emoji (🎬/🧪) that screen readers announce.
findings.proposal: In initRunbookTabs add a keydown handler on `bar`: ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move activation and call `btns[id].focus()`, Home/End jump. Set `b.id = "tab-"+t.id`, `b.setAttribute("aria-controls", t.id)`, and on each section `setAttribute("role","tabpanel")`, `setAttribute("aria-labelledby","tab-"+t.id)`, `tabindex="0"`. Render labels as `🎬 Demo runbook` instead of textContent.

findings.title: Lightbox and feedback dialog are mouse-only and do not manage focus
findings.where: assets/js/app.js initLightbox (`shots.forEach(s => s.addEventListener("click"…`, `d.setAttribute("title","Click to enlarge")`, `lb.setAttribute("role","dialog")`) and initFeedback openDialog/closeDialog; CSS figure.shot img { cursor: zoom-in } style.css:241
findings.problem: Screenshots (`figure.shot img`) and `.diagram-card` divs open the lightbox only on click — neither is focusable, so keyboard users cannot enlarge anything (WCAG 2.1.1). The lightbox has role=dialog but no aria-modal, no accessible name tied to content, focus is never moved into it or restored on close, there is no visible Close button, and the cloned diagram has its aria-labelledby stripped so the enlarged SVG has no name. The feedback overlay lacks role=dialog/aria-modal/aria-labelledby, has no focus trap and does not return focus to the triggering button.
findings.proposal: Wrap each `figure.shot img` and zoomable `.diagram-card svg` in a `<button type="button" class="zoom-btn" aria-label="Enlarge: «alt/title»">` (or add tabindex=0 + role=button + Enter/Space handler in JS). In the lightbox: add `aria-modal="true"`, a visible `<button class="lb-close" aria-label="Close">×</button>`, set `aria-label` on the clone from the original `<title>` text, move focus to the close button on open and back to the opener on close, and trap Tab inside. Apply the same role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby (h3 id) and focus-return to `.fb-overlay`. Replace the `title` tooltip with the button's aria-label.

findings.title: Heading levels skip h2 → h4 on 90 of 94 pages and h1 → h3 on whatsnew.html
findings.where: Library convention from _extract/BUILD-GUIDE.md (steps `<li><h4>`, `.benefit h4`); grep: `python3 -c` over usecases/*.html finds 165 skips across 90 pages (e.g. usecases/access-third-party.html: h2 "How to run the demo" → h4 "Set the scene…"; h2 "Removing risk…" → h3 → h4 fine, but h2 "Demo" → h4 is the common pattern). whatsnew.html: 0 h2, 160 h3 directly under h1 (generated by _extract/whatsnew.py).
findings.problem: Screen-reader users navigating by heading level (the most common AT navigation mode) hit a missing level in every demo runbook and benefit grid; whatsnew.html has 160 orphaned h3s. Fails WCAG 1.3.1 / 2.4.10 best practice and makes the heading-list view misleading.
findings.proposal: Retarget the two convention selectors to h3: change `.steps > li h4` and `.benefit h4` in style.css to `.steps > li h3, .steps > li h4` / `.benefit h3, .benefit h4` (keeps old pages rendering), then run a one-off sed over usecases/*.html turning `<li>\n<h4>` inside `ol.steps` and `.benefit … <h4>` into h3 where no h3 precedes them under the same section (script in _extract, verified by the heading-skip check above). Update BUILD-GUIDE.md to say "step titles are h3". In _extract/whatsnew.py emit `<h2>` per entry (add `.wn-card h2{font-size:1.12rem}`), and add the skip-check to _extract/verify.sh as check 9.

findings.title: Focus indicators are missing or fail 3:1 contrast; new diagram kit removes them entirely
findings.where: assets/css/style.css: `.phase-player:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--green-300) }` (345), `.fb-dialog input:focus` (407), `.filter-bar input[type="search"]:focus` (460), `.deck-picker-search:focus` (739) all use --green-300; no `:focus-visible` rule exists for .btn, .filter-btn, .rb-tab, .toc a, .uc-card, .nav-link, .theme-toggle, .fb-btn, .pager a, .phase-dot/.phase-prev/.phase-next; dg-kit block `.x-mod, .x-hs, .x-persona, .x-ln, .x-goview, .x-ch { outline: none }` (style.css 925–1116, uncommitted)
findings.problem: Computed from the tokens: --green-300 #6cc9ae against --surface #fbfdfc is 1.94:1 and against --page 1.82:1 in light mode (WCAG 2.4.11/2.4.13 require 3:1 for the focus indicator). Everything else relies on the UA default ring, which is 1px Chrome blue-on-navy in the topnav/hero and nearly invisible on `.uc-card` (hover transform masks it). The diagram-kit rules set `outline:none` on `cursor:pointer` groups — the classic anti-pattern.
findings.proposal: Add one global rule near the top of style.css: `:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--green-600); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; }` plus `.topnav :focus-visible, .hero :focus-visible, .deck-tray :focus-visible { outline-color: #7ee0bf; }` (7.9:1 on navy). Replace every `var(--green-300)` in the focus rules with `var(--green-600)` (3.6:1 light, 7.4:1 dark). Delete the six `outline: none` declarations from the dg-kit block (or in _extract/diagram-kit/glue.css so the generated block inherits it).

findings.title: Small grey/kicker text falls below 4.5:1 in light mode
findings.where: assets/css/style.css tokens: --ink-3 #6f7d77 on --page #f2f6f4 = 3.95:1 (used by .pager .dir .76rem (498), .toc-title .74rem (167), .result-count (468), .cat-count (489), .vert-label (141)); --ink-3 on --surface #fbfdfc = 4.22:1 (figure.shot figcaption .84rem (243), .diagram-caption (277), .phase-dot .8rem (359), .dg-tiny 11px (282), .deck-selected-caption); .section-kicker --green-600 #0e8a6d on --page = 3.95:1 at .76rem bold (173); .deck-picker-cat same (745–748)

findings.title: 1,043 external links open new tabs with no warning; ambiguous repeated link texts
findings.where: grep `target="_blank"` over usecases/*.html = 1043, only 1 page mentions "new tab". Repeated identical text with different hrefs: usecases/security-iso27001.html:329–334 five links reading just "KB"; usecases/migration-methodology.html 15 links reading "Policy"; usecases/access-app-connectors.html 3 × "Guide"; usecases/security-inbound-ips.html 2 × "the KB"; usecases/ai-threat-landscape.html 2 × "GenAI Visibility Assessment" (different targets)
findings.problem: WCAG 3.2.5/G201: opening a new window without notice disorients screen-reader and cognitively impaired users. "KB" ×5 / "Policy" ×15 in a links list are indistinguishable (WCAG 2.4.4 link purpose).
findings.proposal: Library-wide, in style.css: `a[target="_blank"]::after{content:" ↗";font-size:.8em;text-decoration:none}` plus a visually-hidden suffix added once in app.js: for each `a[target=_blank]` append ` (opens in a new tab)` and add `.sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0 0 0 0);white-space:nowrap}`. Rewrite the repeated texts: iso27001 → "KB: Posture Compliance Report", "KB: posture checks", etc.; methodology → "Policy deep-dive: Palo Alto" (or `aria-label="Palo Alto policy deep-dive"`); app-connectors → "Guide: App Connector sizing" etc. Add a verify.sh check that flags identical link text with >1 distinct href in a page.

findings.title: 255 data tables: no th scope, 56 use <td><strong> as row headers, none has a caption, scroll wrappers not keyboard-reachable
findings.where: grep `<th scope` = 0 of 978 `<th>`; `<caption` = 0; python scan finds 56 tables whose first column is `<td><strong>…` (e.g. usecases/demo-platform-60.html:304 bridge-lines table, migration-*-policy rule-mapping tables); `.table-wrap { overflow-x: auto }` (style.css:437) has no tabindex
findings.problem: Without scope, screen readers still infer column headers in simple tables, but the 56 row-header tables announce each cell with only the column header, losing the row context ("Say: …" without which bridge). And: "Thirty minutes before a Palo Alto displacement meeting I want to drill the eight objections I'll hear." findings.title: Demo timer overlay and presenter mode for runbooks (segment clock + 60-minute master clock)
findings.where: Timing markup already exists but in two forms: demo-swg.html lines 234-265 uses ranges (`0:00 – 2:00`), demo-ztna.html 212-233 and the other five segment pages use durations (`1 min`); demo-platform-60.html `section#timeline` (lines ~96-175) holds the minute slots (`00–05`, `10–15`…) and `section#late` the cut plan. app.js `initRunbookTabs()` is where the control would be injected; `section#demo ol.steps li` is the step model on 72 pages.
findings.problem: User story: "I'm presenting segment 3 of the 60-minute demo; I want to know I have 90 seconds left in this segment and that I'm still inside minute 20–25 of the hour, without looking at a phone." The 60-minute page says "Start the clock when the last expected attendee joins" and "the running order does not stretch" but gives the SE nothing to run the clock with. Steps also have no presenter view — the SE scrolls a long page in front of a customer.
findings.proposal: 1) Normalise timing markup first (small fix): one form, `1 min`, on all 7 segment pages; document in BUILD-GUIDE's demo-section rules. 2) `initDemoTimer()` in app.js: when `section#demo .steps li h4 .tag[data-min]` exists, add a `⏱ Start` button to the `.rb-tabs` bar; running state shows a fixed bottom-left pill (reuse `.deck-tray` styling) with elapsed/remaining for the current step and total, highlights the current `li` (`.steps li.now`), goes amber at 100% and red at 120%; Space pauses, N/→ advances, Esc stops. 3) Master clock: on demo-platform-60 the `#timeline` table rows carry `data-slot="10-15"`; starting the master clock stores `{t0, slot}` in `sessionStorage["uc-demo-clock"]`; segment pages read it and show "Hour: 22:14 — segment 3 ends at 25:00", so navigating page-to-page keeps one clock. When the hour runs behind, the pill links to `#late` (the cut plan). 4) Presenter mode (`P` key or button): `body.presenter` hides TOC/hero/resources, shows one step at a time at large type with the `.path` chip prominent, ←/→ to move; it is ~40 lines of CSS on existing markup. Build: ~250 lines JS, ~80 CSS. Risks: no-op safely when the markup is absent (prospect build strips `#demo` and the JS still loads); sessionStorage is per-tab — document that the segments must be opened in the same tab (the 60-min page links are same-tab already); keep the timer purely client-side (no audio) to avoid surprising the room.

findings.title: Competitive quick-compare matrix across the 15 vendor playbooks
findings.where: 17 `section#mapping` tables ("«Vendor» component | Cato equivalent | Migration note" on 12 pages; outliers: migration-zscaler.html 'Zscaler object | Cato destination', migration-sophos.html 'Stays in Sophos Central | Moves to Cato', migration-cisco-asa.html 'Model | Last order …'), 14 `#gotchas`, and the 15 `migration-*-policy.html` deep-dives with fixed `#swg / #casb / #dlp / #fw-rules` sections (15 each). planner-rules.js already enumerates vendors as dimensions (proxy / fw / sdwan / ra). Today that is three or four 600-line pages read side by side; multi-vendor estates (the common case, and exactly what planner.html captures) have no comparative view at all.

Risks: accuracy and FUD — restrict cell text to what the pages already say and show the source anchor on every cell; keep competitive content out of the prospect edition (strip page + JS in build-prospect.py); 15 columns overflow at phone width — collapse to a per-vendor accordion under 900px (verify.sh step 6 checks 390px overflow on every page).

findings.title: Glossary with hover definitions and a glossary page
findings.where: 0 `<abbr>` tags in 94 pages (grep -o '<abbr' usecases/*.html | wc -l → 0). The library assumes Cato vocabulary throughout; partners and new hires are explicitly in the audience (README line 1) and have no in-library reference.

findings.title: Offline-ready install (web manifest + service worker) — blocked on HTTPS, so pair with a visible 'take it offline' path
findings.where: No `serviceWorker`, `manifest` or `sw.js` anywhere (grep -rl serviceWorker index.html planner.html assets/js usecases → nothing). Hosting is plain HTTP at http://10.7.0.4:8080 (README Hosting section; _extract/server.py with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, line 42). Distribution zips exist (`_extract/package.sh` full ~58 MB / lite ~12 MB) but are not linked from the UI.
findings.problem: User story: "On a customer site without the Cato tunnel the hosted library is unreachable; I want the copy I opened yesterday to still work." Browsers only register a service worker on HTTPS or localhost, so the obvious 'add a SW' answer does nothing on 10.7.0.4:8080 — and `Cache-Control: no-cache` plus 42 MB of `assets/img` means the browser cache will not carry the SE through either.
findings.proposal: Two-step. (a) Cheap and certain now: when `location.protocol` is http(s), app.js adds a `⬇ Offline copy` nav-link pointing at `dist/sase-use-case-library-lite.zip` (have deploy.sh run `package.sh lite` and rsync `dist/` to the web root; serve it; keep it out of git via the existing `dist/` ignore) with a one-line 'unzip → open index.html' hint; the lite edition is already file://-safe. (b) Proper: put TLS on the host (Caddy or nginx reverse-proxying server.py on 8443 with the Cato-issued or an internal CA cert that SE laptops already trust), then add `manifest.webmanifest` (name, theme colour #0e8a6d, the existing SVG favicon rasterised) and `sw.js` generated by `_extract/build-sw.py`: precache `index.html, planner.html, assets/css/style.css, assets/js/*.js, usecases/*.html` (~3 MB) with a content-hash version; `assets/img/*` cache-on-first-view (stale-while-revalidate), `/api/feedback` network-only. Register only on `https:`. Build: (a) ~20 lines; (b) ~120 lines Python/JS plus host work. Risks: (b) is useless without HTTPS — state this in README so nobody ships a SW that silently never registers; SW caching fights the `no-cache` release policy unless the precache list is versioned per deploy (build-sw.py should stamp the git SHA and deploy.sh should regenerate it); the full 42 MB image set must stay lazy or the first install stalls.

findings.title: Atom feed for the changelog plus a 'new since your last visit' badge
findings.where: _extract/whatsnew.py lines 9-24 already parse `git log` into `(date, subject, bullets)` entries and emit only whatsnew.html; index.html topnav links "What's new" (line 27); no `*.xml` in the root; build-prospect.py excludes whatsnew (WHATSNEW_LINK_RE).

findings.title: Per-page feedback exists (hosted only) — add section anchors, a one-click useful/not vote and a file:// fallback
findings.where: app.js `initFeedback()` (bails unless `location.protocol` is http/https; posts `{type,name,message,page}` to `/api/feedback`); _extract/server.py `do_POST` lines 50-75 writes `stamp | KIND | name | page | message` to feedback-log.txt; README says read it with `ssh … cat feedback-log.txt`. No feedback path in the zip/file:// editions; no per-section granularity; no low-friction signal.
findings.problem: Confirmed present and working, but: (1) an SE using the zip or the prospect-edition clone has no button at all; (2) "the DLP step is wrong" arrives without which step — `page` is `location.pathname` only; (3) a free-text dialog with a mandatory name is the right bar for bugs but too high for "this runbook worked in the room", which is the signal that would tell the maintainer which of the 72 runbooks to invest in (and which capture-wanted mock-ups to replace first).
findings.proposal: (a) Include `location.hash` and the nearest `section[id]` (reuse the IntersectionObserver `current` from initPage) in the payload and the dialog's note ("Logged against #pov on …"). (b) Hover-reveal 👍/👎 on each `.section-kicker` posting `{type:"vote", page, section, value}` to the same endpoint (server.py: `kind = "VOTE"`; no name required for votes, rate-limit one per section per session via sessionStorage); render the kinds in a tiny `_extract/feedback-report.py` that summarises the log by page/section so the maintainer no longer reads raw lines. (c) On file://, show the buttons anyway and fall back to `mailto:tstalker95@gmail.com?subject=[UC library] …&body=<prefilled page/section>` (address pulled from a `data-feedback-mailto` attribute on `<body>` set at package time, never in the prospect build). (d) Add the demo-timer's "ran this demo" end event as an automatic vote so runbook usage is measured without asking. Build: ~80 lines JS, ~20 Python each. Risks: votes without names are not traceable — keep names mandatory for text, optional for votes and say so in README; the log format gains a kind — update the README read-it-with line and the 403 BLOCKED list is unaffected.

findings.title: Library-wide search from every page (Ctrl/Cmd-K command palette)
findings.where: `#uc-search` exists only in index.html (line 110); `grep -c uc-search usecases/access-third-party.html` → 0; search-index.js (99 lines, loaded by index.html only) already holds the full-text word list per page; app.js `initPage()` builds the TOC but has no search; the only keyboard handling is Escape (lightbox/feedback) and ←/→ in phase players.

findings.title: Make the 1,204 CMA path chips clickable into the SE's own tenant
